title: Liveness Probes – Restart Stuck Apps 🔁
description: Automatically restart containers that have entered a broken state.

slides.title: Why Liveness Probes? 🩺
slides.content:
# Fix deadlocks automatically

A container might still be running but completely stuck – a deadlock, infinite loop, or corrupted state. It won’t crash, so no restart happens. A **liveness probe** catches this.

If the liveness probe fails consecutively (`failureThreshold` times), the kubelet kills the container and (depending on restartPolicy) starts a fresh one.

slides.title: Liveness Probe Configuration 🛠️
slides.content:
## Very similar to readiness

```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 15
  periodSeconds: 20
  failureThreshold: 3
```

- `initialDelaySeconds` – wait before first check (should be longer than the app’s startup time).
- `failureThreshold` – how many failures before restart.
- **Do not check dependencies** in a liveness probe (e.g., an external DB). A flaky DB could restart your app unnecessarily. Liveness should only verify the app’s internal health.

quizData.question: What happens after a liveness probe fails `failureThreshold` times?
quizData.explanation: The kubelet kills the container and creates a new one per the restart policy.

slides.title: Exec-based Liveness Probe 💻
slides.content:
## Run a script inside the container

```yaml
livenessProbe:
  exec:
    command:
    - cat
    - /tmp/healthy
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5
```

This checks for the existence of a file. If the file is removed, the probe fails, and the container is restarted.

slides.title: Demonstrate Liveness
slides.content: Create a Pod that deletes the file after 30 seconds:
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: liveness-exec
spec:
  containers:
  - name: liveness
    image: busybox
    args:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    - touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 30; rm -f /tmp/healthy; sleep 600
    livenessProbe:
      exec:
        command:
        - cat
        - /tmp/healthy
      initialDelaySeconds: 5
      periodSeconds: 5
EOF

quizData.question: True or False: An exec liveness probe succeeds if the command returns a non‑zero exit code.
quizData.explanation: Exit code 0 means success; non‑zero means failure.

slides.title: Liveness Probe Pitfalls ⚠️
slides.content:
## Avoid cascading failures

- Don’t check external services. If your liveness probe hits a downstream API, a network blip could restart all your pods.
- Set `initialDelaySeconds` generously so the container has time to start.
- Use lightweight checks – don’t run heavy computation every few seconds.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use separate endpoints for readiness and liveness

For example, `/healthz` for readiness (includes dependency checks) and `/livez` for liveness (only internal process check).

quizData.question: Which probe should you use to handle a deadlocked process?
quizData.explanation: Liveness restarts the container when the process is stuck.
